passages.quote:
The High Street Rental Auctions Fund provides up to £10 million of grant funding to help local authorities use High Street Rental Auction powers and tackle persistent high street vacancy.

Funding is available to support key stages of delivery, including vacancy registers, consumer market reports, property surveys and refurbishment works to bring eligible vacant premises up to a minimum letting standard.

The fund is designed to accelerate local implementation, bring empty properties back into use more quickly, and support thriving high streets and town centres.

Fund summary

Type of fund: Applications assessed on a rolling basis with early applications prioritised.

Eligibility: Local authorities with planning powers based in England

Funding available: Up to £10 million

Important dates:

Applications open: Week commencing 7 December 2026

Deadline for applications: 31 January 2028 (may close earlier if we allocate all funds before the deadline)

Introduction

The government has published Hope on the High Street, a new strategy for Britain’s high streets. The strategy is backed by a £210 million Community Assets Programme to support local communities in England to reimagine and revive their struggling high streets. This programme aims to tackle vacancy and dereliction, protect valued community assets, support co-operative development, and strengthen local capacity to create more resilient, mixed-use high streets.

As part of the Community Assets Programme, the government is making £10 million available to support councils in England to deliver High Street Rental Auctions (HSRAs). HSRAs are power for local authorities to require landlords to rent out persistently vacant commercial properties to new tenants. They allow local authorities to auction the lease of a commercial high street property that has been vacant for 366 days or more in a 24-month period.

Further guidance: For more information on implementing High Street Rental Auctions, including non-statutory guidance and supporting templates, see the High Street Rental Auctions: Non-statutory guidance. The government intends to update the guidance to reflect emerging delivery experience and support wider use of the powers.

The HSRA fund aims to:

Enable councils to identify and bring forward suitable vacant commercial properties for auction through the development of robust evidence and property pipelines.

Support councils to gather market intelligence, consumer demand data and property information to demonstrate local need, viability and the benefits of bringing vacant premises back into use.

Fund the surveys, assessments and preparatory work required to understand refurbishment needs and enable effective implementation of HSRA powers.

Support targeted refurbishment of properties subject to the High Street Rental Auction process, ensuring premises meet a minimum standard and are capable of attracting occupiers.

Bring long-term vacant commercial premises back into active use, supporting local businesses, community uses and high street regeneration.

Applying for funding

Who can apply?

Funding is available to local authorities in England, including unitary authorities, and Mayoral Combined Authorities supporting councils within their area to deliver HSRAs, particularly where they hold relevant planning powers.

How to apply

Applications for the high street rental auctions fund will open from the week commencing 7 December 2026.

When the fund is live the application portal will be accessed via a link on this page.

Detailed application guidance will be also be made available.

What can you apply for?

You can apply for funding for eligible activity that supports the delivery of HSRA powers as described in the Local Authorities (Rental Auctions) (England) and Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (Amendment) Regulations 2024.

The activity must be delivered within a high street or town centre designated, or being considered for designation, in line with Part 10 of the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023.

Projects must be related to commercial high street premises that are, or may be, eligible for HSRA activity.

You can apply for funding under one or more of the strands set out in this prospectus, subject to meeting the relevant criteria. See Annex A for eligible and ineligible costs.

Refurbishment projects are limited to a maximum of 3 eligible premises per local authority, capped at £200,000 per refurbishment project.

All funded activity must be completed by 31 March 2028. We will not cover expenditure incurred before an eligible application is approved, unless this is expressly permitted.

Funding available

There is up to £10 million available, which we will award on a rolling basis. We will assess applications as we receive them. If your application meets the criteria for funding and funds are still available, we will send you a funding offer.

We’ve estimated the costs of works and services, which you should use as a guide:

vacancy registers will cost approximately £3,000 to £8,000

property condition surveys will cost approximately £1,000 to £3,000

high street feasibility research, and consumer market approximately £3,000 to £8,000

We will consider costs above these estimates but need to understand why your costs are higher.

We encourage you to secure match funding from the landlord of the property for refurbishment projects, however this is not a requirement.

How applications will be assessed

You will only receive funding if your application passes eligibility checks and funding remains available.

We will check:

that you are applying from a local authority with planning powers in England

which funding strand you are applying under

that the proposed activity supports HSRA delivery

that your property has been vacant for 366 days in the last 2 years (for refurbishment projects)

that you have provided the required evidence and delivery information
